assets.protection_goal: No observation or evidence artifact may inherit proposal or execution authority.
Every admitted observation remains traceable to source, review, timestamp, unit, and content hash.
Accepted captures remain immutable and deterministically replayable.
Gate promotion remains a separate explicit human act.

residual_risks.description: The live campaign used one Sepolia Blockscout instance; transport stability is proven, independent live truth is not.
residual_risks.treatment: Keep conclusions source-specific, use the offline consensus tribunal for future multi-source admission, and require a separately reviewed mainnet source set before Gate 1B.

residual_risks.description: DNS, endpoint behavior, rate limits, terms, and response contracts remain controlled by an external provider.
residual_risks.treatment: Time-bound source review, stop on drift, re-review by 2026-09-04T01:12:00Z, and preserve rollback.

residual_risks.description: Provider-reported counters and gas fields are workflow observations, not executable prices or profitability proof.
residual_risks.treatment: Require explicit translation, assumptions, missing-economics disclosure, local simulation, and no live proposal routing.

threats.mitigation: Fail closed, emit rollback evidence, stop the run, and preserve the last valid replay corpus.
threats.scenario: Reviewed endpoint is unavailable, times out, or fails during a bounded capture.

threats.mitigation: Require reviewed DNS hostname, public-address enforcement, preflight and postflight comparison, and transport-level connection pinning while retaining TLS hostname verification.
threats.scenario: The reviewed hostname resolves to non-public or changed addresses between preflight and postflight.

threats.mitigation: Reject cross-host redirects and stop the capture.
threats.scenario: A redirect attempts to leave the exact reviewed host.

threats.mitigation: Verify raw and normalized SHA-256 values, canonical artifact IDs, and replay hashes; fail closed on mismatch.
threats.scenario: Persisted raw, normalized, or replay artifacts are changed after capture.

threats.mitigation: Enforce per-observation TTL and refuse mixed fresh/stale evidence with HOLD_STALE.
threats.scenario: An expired observation is admitted or borrows freshness from another source.

threats.mitigation: Enforce content type, parser, response-size, and schema boundaries; reject without retrying into authority.
threats.scenario: The source returns malformed, unsupported, or oversized content.

threats.mitigation: Run targeted secret-name preflight, require no wallet/signing credentials, and keep connector methods GET/HEAD only.
threats.scenario: Write-capable credentials are present in the environment or become reachable by the read-only lane.

threats.mitigation: Fix authority fields and counts at false/zero, assert downstream gates locked, and reject command-shaped artifacts.
threats.scenario: An observation, fixture, report, or evidence artifact is interpreted as permission to propose, sign, transact, execute, or move capital.

threats.mitigation: Preserve each observation and conflict magnitude; return HOLD_CONFLICT without averaging.
threats.scenario: Admissible sources disagree beyond a declared tolerance.

threats.mitigation: Return HOLD_CONCENTRATION and keep aggregate_value null.
threats.scenario: Agreeing surfaces share one provider or provenance group and masquerade as independent corroboration.

threats.mitigation: Allow only explicit identity or decimal-scale conversions; return HOLD_UNIT_AMBIGUITY otherwise.
threats.scenario: Values use unknown units, decimals, or implicit conversions.

threats.mitigation: Require eligible time-bounded review and return HOLD_SOURCE_REVIEW or HOLD_REVIEW_EXPIRED.
threats.scenario: A source remains reachable after its review expires or its contract changes.

threats.mitigation: Limit the conclusion to transport/replay stability, preserve the concentration warning, and keep Gate 1B and Gate 2 locked.
threats.scenario: The live Gate 1A campaign uses one Blockscout Sepolia instance and therefore cannot establish independent live corroboration.

trust_boundaries.rule: HTTPS GET only to the exact reviewed host and port 443 after DNS/public-IP preflight.
Raw and normalized hashes, parser lineage, TTL, and postflight resolution must verify.
Observed values, deterministic transforms, assumptions, and missing economics remain separate.
Evidence may support human review but may not create proposals, commands, signatures, transactions, execution, or capital movement.

What source-specific outage and deprecation behavior must be re-tested after the current review expires?
Should later source sets require provider, infrastructure, and data-origin diversity as separate dimensions?
